title: GulfDrive Weekly: 2025 Meridian Solara XLE Hybrid road test
author: GulfDrive Weekly
text:
We spent a week with the 2025 Meridian Solara XLE Hybrid on UAE roads, from Dubai traffic to the run up Jebel Jais.

The hybrid powertrain pairs a 2.5-litre four-cylinder engine with an electric motor for a combined 225 horsepower, sent to the front wheels through an e-CVT. Peak torque is 221 Nm. Meridian claims 0-100 km/h in 7.8 seconds, and it feels every bit that quick off the line.

Fuel economy is the headline: the official combined figure is 23.8 km/l, and around town the brochure promises 25 km/l. The 50-litre tank means fewer stops than you would expect.

At 4,920 mm long with a 2,825 mm wheelbase, the Solara is a big sedan, and the 428-litre boot swallowed our luggage easily. It weighs about 1,650 kg.

The cabin feels genuinely premium and the ride is plush over broken tarmac. The steering is light but vague.

Equipment is generous: nine airbags, adaptive cruise control and a 360-degree camera are standard, and the panoramic sunroof comes as standard too. Ventilated front seats are standard, which matters in a Gulf summer. A head-up display is optional.

Meridian backs it with a five-year warranty.

title: Owner forum: 3 months with my 2025 Solara hybrid, some corrections
author: u/desert_commuter
text:
Three months and 9,000 km into my UAE-spec 2025 Meridian Solara XLE Hybrid, so here are some real numbers.

A lot of reviews repeat that it makes 230 horsepower. The dealer brochure I was given says the same thing, and honestly it feels strong enough.

Fuel economy is where I disagree with the magazines. The official combined figure is 20 km/l, not the fantasy numbers you see quoted.

It does 0-100 km/h in 7.8 seconds, which matches my own timing. Top speed is 210 km/h according to the salesman.

The boot is 428 litres and the car is 1,840 mm wide, so check your garage. Ground clearance is only 145 mm.

My car has all-wheel drive, which is great in the rain.

There is no head-up display at all on this trim, which is disappointing at this price.

Blind spot monitor is standard. Wireless phone charger is standard as well.

The seats are comfortable on long trips and the hybrid system is impressively quiet.

The hybrid battery warranty is 10 years.

title: Trailhead TV: 2025 Kestrel Ridgeback, Summit vs Adventure (transcript)
author: Trailhead TV
text:
Welcome back to Trailhead TV. Today we have both versions of the 2025 Kestrel Ridgeback, and these are GCC-spec cars.

Let's start with the Summit. Under the hood is a 3.5-litre V6 making 295 horsepower and 356 Nm of torque. It gets a ten-speed automatic and proper four-wheel drive with low range. It will tow 3,500 kg, and you get 235 mm of ground clearance. It seats seven, and a locking rear differential is standard.

The Adventure is a different animal. It uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder with 245 horsepower, and it's all-wheel drive only. Kestrel says the Adventure will do 0-100 km/h in 6.9 seconds, and it returns 11 km/l combined. Towing is limited to 2,500 kg on the Adventure. You can't get a third row in the Adventure, and there's no locking rear differential either.

Both cars are 4,890 mm long and 1,930 mm wide.

Honestly, the Summit feels unstoppable off-road, while the Adventure is the nicer daily driver.

Fuel economy on the Summit is rough: 9.6 km/l combined, and the tank is 80 litres. The Summit has a top speed of 220 km/h.

title: Voltkreis: 2024 Voltaire E-Line Long Range review
author: Voltkreis
text:
The 2024 Voltaire E-Line Long Range is the version most European buyers will choose, and after 1,200 km on German roads it is easy to see why.

The rear motor produces 210 kW, which is 282 hp, and 350 Nm of torque. The sprint from 0-100 km/h takes 6.1 seconds and top speed is limited to 180 km/h.

The battery has 77 kWh of usable capacity and the WLTP range is 580 km. It can fast charge at up to 170 kW.

At 1,960 kg it is no lightweight, but the 440-litre boot is practical. It is rear-wheel drive and uses a single-speed transmission.

A heat pump is standard, as is the panoramic glass roof, and vehicle-to-load is included. A head-up display is standard too.

The Standard Range makes do with a 58 kWh battery and 435 km of range.

The ride is firm but well controlled, and the cabin is impressively quiet at speed.

The battery is covered by an eight-year warranty.

title: Used buy: should you get a 2023 Meridian Solara?
author: SecondOwner
text: Thinking about a used 2023 Meridian Solara SE? The 2023 Meridian Solara SE makes 203 hp and has a 60-litre fuel tank. It is a comfortable, sensible commuter.

title: Continental Motoring: 2025 Meridian Solara Excel Hybrid first drive
author: Continental Motoring
text:
The 2025 Meridian Solara Excel Hybrid has finally arrived in Europe. System output is 218 PS, and WLTP combined consumption is 4.8 l/100km. That works out to roughly 49 mpg, which is excellent for a car this size.

It weighs 1,655 kg and reaches 100 km/h from rest in 8.4 seconds.

Eight airbags are standard, and the head-up display is standard. A panoramic sunroof costs extra. There are no ventilated front seats.

The warranty runs for five years.

The interior is classy, though the infotainment is laggy.
